wrong_choice_explanations: を marks the object of an action; 五時 is not something you 'work', so 五時を働きます is ungrammatical. The end time takes まで.
と means 'and/with'; 五時と働きます would treat five o'clock like a coworker. The end of the working time needs まで.
が marks the subject; 五時 can't be the one who works. まで is needed to show 'until five'.

exercises.example_sentence: 駅まで歩いて行きました。
exercises.translation: I walked all the way to the station.
wrong_choice_explanations: で marks where an action happens (駅で = 'at the station'), but with 歩いて行きました the sentence needs the goal that is reached, which is what まで marks.
と means 'with' (友達と歩く); the station is not a walking companion, so 駅と歩いて行きました makes no sense. The goal 'as far as the station' is まで.
が marks the subject; the station can't be the one walking. まで shows how far you walked.

exercises.example_sentence: 月曜日から日曜日まで忙しいです。
exercises.translation: I'm busy from Monday until Sunday.
wrong_choice_explanations: に marks a single point in time (日曜日に); after 月曜日から the sentence needs the end of the period, 'until Sunday', which is まで.
を marks a direct object; 日曜日 is not an object of 忙しい, so 日曜日を忙しい is ungrammatical.
と means 'and' (月曜日と日曜日 = Monday and Sunday); it can't follow 〜から to close a 'from … until' range.
exercises.hiragana_full: げつようびからにちようびまでいそがしいです。

exercises.example_sentence: 宿題が終わるまで寝られません。
exercises.translation: I can't sleep until I finish my homework.
wrong_choice_explanations: と makes an automatic 'whenever' result (終わると = 'when it finishes'), but the sentence needs the durational 'until it finishes' that まで provides.
なら sets up a hypothetical 'if' (終わるなら = 'if it is going to finish'), not the time limit 'until' that まで expresses.
から gives a reason (終わるから = 'because it finishes'), but here まで marks the endpoint up to which you cannot sleep.

exercises.example_sentence: 図書館は夜八時まで開いています。
exercises.translation: The library is open until eight at night.
wrong_choice_explanations: で can mark when something ends with 終わる/閉まる (八時で閉まる), but with 開いています ('is open') it can't show how long; that is まで.
を marks a direct object; 八時 is not an object of 開いています, so 八時を開いています is ungrammatical.
と means 'and/with'; 夜八時と開いています makes no sense. The closing time 'until eight' is まで.

exercises.example_sentence: 夏休みは八月三十一日までです。
wrong_choice_explanations: に marks the time when something happens (八月三十一日に行きます); it can't be followed directly by です to say how long the vacation lasts.
で marks place or means; 八月三十一日でです is ungrammatical. The last day of the vacation is shown with まで.
を marks a direct object and can't come before です; 八月三十一日をです is ungrammatical.

exercises.example_sentence: 一時から三時まで昼休みです。
exercises.translation: Lunch break is from one to three o'clock.
wrong_choice_explanations: に marks a single point in time (三時に); after 一時から the sentence needs the end of the break, 'until three', which is まで.
で marks place or means; 三時で昼休みです doesn't express the end of a time range. Use まで.
を marks a direct object; 三時 is not an object here, so 三時を昼休みです is ungrammatical.

exercises.example_sentence: 雨がやむまで外で遊べません。
exercises.translation: We can't play outside until the rain stops.
wrong_choice_explanations: 間 ('while/during') covers the whole stretch of time the rain continues, but まで pins down the endpoint — you cannot play up to the moment it stops.
と makes an automatic result (やむと = 'when it stops'), describing what happens at that point rather than the 'until' span that まで marks.
うちに means 'while (a state still lasts)', pointing to doing something during a period, not waiting up to the endpoint that まで marks.

exercises.example_sentence: 病院までお見舞いに行きました。
exercises.translation: I went to the hospital to visit (someone).
wrong_choice_explanations: で marks where an action happens (病院で = 'at the hospital'), but with 行きました the sentence needs the destination reached, which まで marks.
と means 'with' (友達と行く); the hospital is not a companion, so 病院とお見舞いに行きました makes no sense. The destination takes まで.
を doesn't mark the destination of 行きます; 病院をお見舞いに行きました is ungrammatical. まで shows where you went.

exercises.example_sentence: 十二時まで起きていました。
exercises.translation: I stayed awake until twelve o'clock.
wrong_choice_explanations: を marks a direct object; 十二時 is not an object of 起きていました, so 十二時を起きていました is ungrammatical.
で marks place or means; 十二時で起きていました doesn't say how long you stayed up. The end point 'until twelve' is まで.
と means 'and/with'; 十二時と起きていました makes no sense. Use まで for 'until twelve'.
